roles.Rule: One demanding but teachable reference that gives coherent structure.
Original paper/text/data/artifact when the field has a meaningful primary-source tradition.
roles.Why: Lets learners see what later summaries changed.

roles.Rule: A serious alternative theory, interpretation, design tradition, or critique.
roles.Why: Prevents the spine from becoming invisible orthodoxy.

roles.Rule: An earlier model that was useful but limited, where pedagogically valuable.
roles.Why: Shows why ideas changed and what problems they solved.

roles.Rule: Current review, handbook, or advanced text that updates the field.
roles.Why: Prevents historical canon from freezing knowledge.

roles.Rule: A real event, experiment, system failure, institution, lawsuit, design, or controversy.
Material from another region/tradition/institutional form when the domain could otherwise provincialize.
Dataset, map, proof, codebase, building, painting, performance, specimen, machine, archive, or other non-prose object.
Encyclopedia, standard, handbook, glossary, atlas, code, API spec, legal text, or database.
Prefer legal open/public-domain editions when quality is adequate; do not lower intellectual quality merely to force everything free.
roles.Why: Keeps the open curriculum usable while respecting source licenses.

roles.Rule: For selected important works, read whole books/plays/papers rather than only excerpts or summaries.
roles.Why: Builds stamina, context, memory, and encounter with extended argument/form.

roles.Rule: Record claim, question, passage locator, disagreement, connection, and what changed in the learner's model.
